text:
Varsovie le 1/13 Mars 1832 No. 2216
Monsieur [Schmidt]!
En me référant à l’office que j’ai eu l’honneur de Vous adresser le 31 Janvier/12 Février dernier Nro. 1871 je m’empresse de Vous prévenir que c’est Monsieur le Conseiller d’Etat Joseph Lubowidzki Président de la Banque de Pologne qui vient d’être chargé, d’ordre de Sa Majesté l’Empereur et Roi mon Maître, de la mise à exécution des stipulations de la Convention du 17/29 Mai 1830 et qu’il a reçu les instructions necessaires sous ce rapport.
J’ai tout lieu d’espérer que ce nouveau Commissaire, qui est également autorisé à applanir les questions qui dérivent de la prétention élevée par le Banquier Weigel, saura justifier la confiance de Sa Majesté Impériale et Royale, en s’efforçant à noter, en ce qui dépendra de Lui, l’ajustement de tous les points qui ont besoin d’être définitivement réglés entre le Gouvernement de Pologne et celui de Sa Majesté le Roi de Prusse.
Veuillez, Monsieur, agréer l’expression empressée de ma considération très distinguée.
signé Engel.

translation.en:
Warsaw, 1/13 March 1832 No. 2216

Sir [Schmidt]!

Referring to the communication which I had the honour to address to you on 31 January/12 February last, No. 1871, I hasten to inform you that it is Mr Joseph Lubowidzki, Councillor of State, President of the Bank of Poland, who has just been charged, by order of His Majesty the Emperor and King my Master, with putting into execution the stipulations of the Convention of 17/29 May 1830, and that he has received the necessary instructions in this regard.

I have every reason to hope that this new Commissioner, who is likewise authorised to smooth out the questions that derive from the claim raised by the Banker Weigel, will know how to justify the confidence of His Imperial and Royal Majesty, by striving to note, in so far as it depends on him, the adjustment of all the points which need to be definitively settled between the Government of Poland and that of His Majesty the King of Prussia.

Pray accept, Sir, the eager expression of my most distinguished consideration.

signed Engel.

text_english:
Warsaw, 1/13 March 1832 No. 2216

Sir [Schmidt]!

Referring to the communication which I had the honour to address to you on 31 January/12 February last, No. 1871, I hasten to inform you that it is Mr Joseph Lubowidzki, Councillor of State, President of the Bank of Poland, who has just been charged, by order of His Majesty the Emperor and King my Master, with putting into execution the stipulations of the Convention of 17/29 May 1830, and that he has received the necessary instructions in this regard.

I have every reason to hope that this new Commissioner, who is likewise authorised to smooth out the questions that derive from the claim raised by the Banker Weigel, will know how to justify the confidence of His Imperial and Royal Majesty, by striving to note, in so far as it depends on him, the adjustment of all the points which need to be definitively settled between the Government of Poland and that of His Majesty the King of Prussia.

Pray accept, Sir, the eager expression of my most distinguished consideration.

signed Engel.
summary_en: Copy of a letter from Engel at Warsaw to the consul general Schmidt (no. 2216). Referring to his note of 12 February (no. 1871), he reports that the councillor of state Joseph Lubowidzki, president of the Bank of Poland, has been charged by order of the Emperor and King with carrying out the convention of 29 May 1830 and has received the necessary instructions. This new commissioner is also authorised to settle the questions arising from the claim of the banker Weigel. Engel hopes he will justify the Emperor's confidence and work for the adjustment of every point still to be finally settled between the government of Poland and that of the King of Prussia.
summary_de: Abschrift eines Schreibens Engels aus Warschau an den Generalkonsul Schmidt (Nr. 2216). Unter Bezug auf sein Schreiben vom 12. Februar (Nr. 1871) teilt er mit, dass der Staatsrat Joseph Lubowidzki, Präsident der Bank von Polen, auf Befehl des Kaisers und Königs mit der Ausführung der Konvention vom 29. Mai 1830 beauftragt ist und die nötigen Anweisungen erhalten hat. Dieser neue Kommissar sei auch ermächtigt, die Fragen zu bereinigen, die sich aus der Forderung des Bankiers Weigel ergeben. Engel hofft, er werde das Vertrauen des Kaisers rechtfertigen und sich um die Regelung aller Punkte bemühen, die zwischen der Regierung von Polen und der des Königs von Preußen noch endgültig zu ordnen sind.
